brief.headline: Memory Super Cycle Intensifies: DRAM Q2 +58-63% QoQ, HBM3E +20%, DDR5 Margins Now Exceed HBM, CoWoS Still Tight Through 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="11-2,11-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices will rise 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, following Q1's record 90-95% surge, while NAND Flash will jump 70-75% QoQ.</cite> <cite index="2-1,2-10">SK Group Chairman noted HBM carries ~60% margins while standard memory chips reach ~80%, with Micron's DDR5 profitability now exceeding HBM.</cite> <cite index="24-5,24-9">Hyperscalers will collectively spend roughly $700 billion on capex in 2026, nearly double 2025 levels.</cite> <cite index="32-5">NVIDIA reportedly secured over 60% of total CoWoS capacity for 2025-2026, with TSMC expanding but supply remaining constrained.</cite> <cite index="40-1,40-7,40-26">KOSPI surged a record 606.64 points (8.42%) as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix jumped 8.51% and 11.17% respectively, with combined market cap hitting 3,133 trillion won.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="44-3,44-23">Nomura set targets of 590,000 won for Samsung and 4 million won for SK Hynix, applying TSMC-level 20x P/E valuations versus current 6-7x multiples.</cite> <cite index="39-8">Samsung held 35% HBM market share in Q3 2025 versus SK Hynix's 53%.</cite> <cite index="41-10,41-11,41-12">Samsung's FY consensus operating profit rose to 348 trillion won from 301 trillion won a month prior; SK Hynix jumped to 254 trillion won from 207 trillion won.</cite> Samsung catching up on HBM4 qualification but SK Hynix retains pole position through 2026. Both benefit from DDR5 margin windfall offsetting HBM capex intensity. Near-term edge to SK Hynix on mix; Samsung re-rating if HBM4 ramp accelerates H2. Pair spread compressed post-labor deal; watch relative CoWoS allocation and hyperscaler SCA progress.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="2-6">Meaningful new DRAM capacity unlikely to come online until 2027 at earliest, keeping supply constraints elevated.</cite> <cite index="16-22,16-25">Hyperscaler capex projected to exceed $600 billion in 2026, a 40% YoY increase, with HBM consuming 3:1 DDR5 wafer capacity.</cite> <cite index="2-11,2-13">HBM complexity and tight supply have driven conventional DRAM prices higher; risk that Chinese rivals capitalize if Korean firms maintain high-price strategies.</cite> Pricing momentum slowing sequentially but absolute levels remain elevated. Risk of demand destruction in consumer/mobile segments mounting.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-1,7-1">Samsung and SK Hynix hiked HBM3E prices nearly 20% for 2026 deliveries as demand from NVIDIA and hyperscalers outstrips supply.</cite> <cite index="7-2,7-3">HBM3E supply remains tight as both vendors prioritize ramping HBM4 production, with next year's mix forecast at ~55% HBM4 and 45% HBM3E.</cite> <cite index="8-2,8-4">For Nvidia B200 with eight HBM3e stacks, memory alone costs $2,400, exceeding logic die cost; HBM3E pricing ~$300/stack, HBM4 ~$500/stack.</cite> <cite index="8-11">Lead times for HBM3E stacks remain at 20-26 weeks.</cite> HBM4 ramp critical battleground H2 2026; Samsung qualification progress with Broadcom/Google TPU positive but NVIDIA allocation still SK Hynix-dominated.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q2 2026 DRAM contract prices to rise 58-63% QoQ, NAND 70-75% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Sequential moderation from Q1's 90-95% DRAM surge but pricing power intact; NAND accelerating faster than DRAM for first time this cycle as enterprise SSD demand absorbs capacity. Supply relief pushed to late 2027.

news_pulse.headline: DDR5 margins reportedly surpass HBM at ~80% vs ~60% as conventional memory prices soar
news_pulse.implication: Conventional DRAM now more profitable than HBM despite lower ASPs due to extreme tightness. Validates Samsung/SK Hynix disciplined supply strategy. Risk: incentivizes Chinese DRAM expansion and potential market share loss if pricing sustained.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers to spend ~$700B capex in 2026, up from ~$400B in 2025
news_pulse.implication: Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet collectively doubling capex YoY with no signs of slowdown. Two-thirds allocated to short-lived assets (GPUs/CPUs with 3-5yr depreciation). Sustains HBM and server DRAM demand through 2026-2027; watch for capex fatigue signals in H2 earnings.

news_pulse.headline: NVIDIA secured >60% of TSMC CoWoS capacity for 2025-2026; AMD, hyperscalers compete for remainder
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS remains bottleneck despite TSMC 33% capacity expansion by 2026. Limits total addressable HBM market for Samsung/SK Hynix; benefits vendors with locked-in Nvidia allocations. TSMC pushing CoPoS panel-level packaging to ease constraints by 2027-2028.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix reach tentative OpenAI Stargate deal for 900K DRAM wafers/month supply
news_pulse.implication: Stargate LOI locks in significant capacity (Samsung P5 fab operational 2028, SK Hynix M15X mid-2027). Provides revenue visibility but ties up wafer starts, reinforcing tight supply for non-hyperscaler customers through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI surges record 606.64 points (+8.42%); Samsung +8.51% to 299,500 won, SK Hynix +11.17% to 1.94M won
news_pulse.implication: Combined Samsung/SK Hynix market cap hit 3,133 trillion won (49% of KOSPI). Retail piling in; 24-25% of existing holders added positions in March despite record highs. Momentum extreme; watch for profit-taking if hyperscaler commentary softens or Chinese DRAM ramps accelerate.

news_pulse.headline: South Korea to launch 18 single-stock leveraged/inverse ETFs on Samsung, SK Hynix May 27
news_pulse.implication: Expected net inflows up to 5.3 trillion won ($3.5B). Amplifies volatility; rebalancing reportedly accounted for 17% of SK Hynix and 10% of Samsung daily volume during May 15 selloff. Technical factor to monitor intraday; increases risk of sharper drawdowns on negative catalysts.

news_pulse.headline: Nomura raises KOSPI target to 10,000-11,000; Samsung 590K won, SK Hynix 4M won on HBM super cycle
news_pulse.implication: Argues Samsung/SK Hynix deserve TSMC-like 20x P/E (vs current 6-7x) as HBM super cycle drives ROE through 2026-2027. Consensus operating profit estimates rising (Samsung 348T won, SK Hynix 254T won). Valuation re-rating narrative gaining traction among sell-side; contrarian risk if pricing cycle peaks sooner than expected.

brief.derivatives_signal: South Korea equity derivatives skew likely tilted toward upside gamma concentration post-May 27 leveraged ETF launch. Options volumes on ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) thin; limited actionable signal. KOSPI 200 futures term structure and put/call skew would clarify institutional hedging appetite but not observable in payload. Near-term risk: leveraged product rebalancing amplifies intraday volatility in both directions. Monitor for capitulation wicks if hyperscaler earnings disappoint or China DRAM capacity announcements surface.
watch_for_next_3h: Any hyperscaler (MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META) commentary on AI capex pacing or memory procurement constraints—directional for H2 HBM/DRAM demand visibility
TSMC CoWoS utilization updates or customer allocation shifts; bottleneck easing = incremental HBM supply, tightening = sustained pricing power
Chinese DRAM (CXMT) capacity expansion announcements or Samsung/SK Hynix pricing stabilization signals—risk to consensus peak-cycle narrative
KOSPI options activity and leveraged ETF flows post-May 27 launch; technical reversal risk if profit-taking accelerates with elevated retail leverage
